articles.body: This article provides the required steps for diagnosing and resolving cases where a merchant reports that their POS is stuck on a downloading screen, shows “No content,” “Content failed to load,” or displays a white screen referencing content downloads. 1. Confirm the Device Version Before taking action, verify that the merchant’s device is running major release 23 . You can confirm this in the "Software" section of the device in EloView. If you see 6.000.0 23 .XXXX, the device is on major release 23 (see photo below). If it is not on major release 23, do not update it. Here is the list of devices on MR-23 2. Check for an Elo Home Crash If the merchant reports a downloading/content loading issue: Check EloView to see the Device Screenshot Compare it to the known Elo Home crash image, and please post in #pathfinder-support if you see this image: If the screen resembles the Elo crash state, proceed to the reboot steps below. 3. First Attempt: Reboot the Device Try the least disruptive fix first. You can reboot the device directly from EloView. If the reboot resolves the content issue and the Mx is brought to the login or PIN screen, you are finished. If not. If you do not have EloView access to this device, simply have the Mx restart their device by holding the power button on the rear of the screen. Step 3b: Reinstall the app If the reboot didn't resolve, delete the content on the device and reinstall the current app version. (IKB) Updating Outdated POS & Kiosk Versions 4. If the Reboot & Reinstall Fails Before attempting more advanced recovery: Download Logs (Required) Download the last 24 hours of logs for Engineering and Elo: It will default to the last 24 hours, but ensure the last 24 hours are indeed captured: Important: Do not proceed to any resets until logs are captured. Share the logs in #pathfinder-support. 5. Perform an Enterprise Reset If: Reboot attempts have failed, and App reinstall has failed, and Logs have been downloaded, …then you may proceed with an enterprise reset . Additional SOP: APK Upgrade Failures If you encounter issues when upgrading APK versions: Always download the last 24 hours of logs before taking any further action. Logs are essential for Engineering triage. Summary Step Action 1 Confirm device is on major release 23 2 Check if the screen matches Elo Home crash 3 Attempt reboot (EloView or manual) & Reinstall 4 If reboot fails → download 24h logs 5 After logs are saved → enterprise reset

articles.title: Kitchen Display System (KDS) User Guide
articles.snippet: The Kitchen Display System (KDS) can improve kitchen efficiency (and reduce need for paper tickets) with a live, digital view of all active orders. It connects directly to your POS and displays incoming orders from all connected channels, including POS, Marketplace, and Online Ordering — in real tim
articles.body: The Kitchen Display System (KDS) can improve kitchen efficiency (and reduce need for paper tickets) with a live, digital view of all active orders. It connects directly to your POS and displays incoming orders from all connected channels, including POS, Marketplace, and Online Ordering — in real time. This guide explains how your KDS works, what to expect, and how it interacts with Live Order Management (LOM) on your POS. 🔧 General Functionality What does the KDS do? Your KDS digitally displays orders as soon as they’re placed, allowing your kitchen team to manage preparation and fulfillment without relying on printed tickets. Each order card shows customer details, items, modifiers, fulfillment type, and any notes. To support variable kitchen setups, expo stations and complex operations, the KDS can be filtered by menu selection (item category), channel and fulfillment type, and item-level status . What order statuses appear on the KDS? In Progress — Orders being prepared. Ready — Orders that are complete. Canceled — Orders that have been canceled. (“Picked Up” is a Live Orders-only status and does not appear on the KDS.) How do you mark an order as Ready? Double-tap the order card. This moves the order from “In Progress” to “Ready.” Can you view completed orders? Yes. Completed orders appear in the Ready tab until it clears at the end of the day. Can you recall or reopen a completed order? Yes. This is a configurable feature available in the KDS Settings. See the Order Flow section for more details. Does KDS track item-level completion? Yes. With item status on KDS, individual items can be marked ready. See Order Flow section for more details. Does the KDS make a sound when new orders arrive? Not currently supported. You’ll need to visually monitor for new order cards. Does the KDS work offline? Yes. It continues receiving orders from the POS via your local network (LAN), but in order for this to work, you must have a functioning LAN. In certain scenarios, your LAN may also be down, in which case your KDS would not work. Additionally, Marketplace or Online Ordering tickets may be delayed until your internet connection is restored. 🧾 Order Flow When do orders appear on KDS? If your setup uses Auto Confirm , orders appear immediately. If your setup uses Manual Confirm , orders appear after you accept them in LOM, or the DoorDash Marketplace tablet (or whatever other order protocol you use). Do scheduled orders appear? Yes. Scheduled orders appear 20 minutes before the pickup time. What happens if an order is updated after being marked Ready? LOM resets the order status to In Progress until the new items are completed. Items already marked Ready stay complete. Kiosk orders If you utilize a self-serve kiosk, orders placed at the kiosk will also show up on the KDS. Saved orders Your saved orders appear on the KDS once they are "Sent to kitchen." If orders are "Saved for Later," they will not appear on the KDS. If new items are added later to a saved order, those items appear as a new card under the same order ID. You should never see duplicate items. What if my order is too long and doesn't fit on the screen? You will see "Continued..." at the bottom of the ticket, and can scroll down to see the rest of the order. Can an order appear on multiple cards? Yes, if new items are added to a saved order. Each new item appears on its own card under the same order ID. How are canceled orders handled? When canceled in LOM, the order card is removed from the KDS immediately. You can identify a canceled order because it will show a Canceled overlay at the top of the order card. What happens if an order is marked Ready on LOM before KDS? Statuses sync automatically. The order will also appear as Ready on KDS and move out of “In Progress.” What happens when a Dasher marks an order as picked up? The order disappears from LOM, but remains visible in the Ready tab on KDS until end of day. Can you clear the Ready tab manually? No. The Ready tab automatically resets overnight. This means double tapping an order in the Ready tab on the KDS will not remove it from the Ready tab. How do I recall an order I accidentally marked as "Ready"? Navigate to Settings where you will see a toggle called "Mark as ready" cancellation timer. When you have this toggled ON, you have five seconds to chancel after tapping to mark an order as ready. Once toggled on, you will see a "Cancel" option available for five seconds after orders are Marked as Ready. 🔄 KDS ↔ LOM Order Flow Scenarios Manual Confirm Orders LOM: You confirm the incoming order. KDS: The order appears under “In Progress.” Mark the order Ready either: From the POS → moves to “Ready” on both POS and KDS From KDS (double-tap) → same result Once the order is handed off, mark “Picked Up” in LOM (no action needed on KDS). Auto Confirm Orders LOM: Orders automatically confirm and move to “Mark Ready for Pickup.” KDS: The order appears under “In Progress.” Mark the order Ready via POS or double-tap on KDS. When the order is picked up, mark “Picked Up” in LOM (no further action in KDS). 🧩 Integrations & Connectivity Does KDS show Marketplace and Online Orders? Yes. KDS displays orders from connected channels as long as they are integrated through LOM. Does the KDS integrate with multiple POS devices? Yes. Any status change (marking Ready, confirming, etc.) syncs across all POS terminals and the KDS in real time. Does the KDS work with printers? Yes. You can continue using printed tickets alongside KDS if preferred. ⚙️ Configuration & Customization There are a number of customizations available on your KDS that allow you to control what you see, don't see, and how orders are displayed. The KDS supports filtering by Item Category, Fulfillment Type, Channel (Marketplace, Online Ordering, In-store), and sorting by time (Oldest or Most recent first). Can you change how order cards look? No. The layout is standardized for readability and consistency. Can you change when tickets turn yellow or red? No, these thresholds are fixed, though we hope to support configurable timers in the future! Yellow: order is about 10 minutes old (running behind) Red: order is about 20 minutes old (late) Can you remove (86) items directly from the KDS? No. 86’ing must be done from your POS. Can you tag or prioritize orders (e.g. “Rush”)? Not supported at this time. Can you recall deleted or canceled saved orders? No. Once removed, these cannot be reopened. How do I configure filter settings on the KDS? Click on the "hamburger" menu (three stacked horizontal lines) on the KDS and click into Settings. From here, you'll see options to filter by: Item Category Fulfillment Type Channel Order Routing allows you to filter by Channel and Fulfillment Type: Item Routing allows you to filter based on Item Category: If I have multiple KDS and I update filters on one, will they be the same on other devices? No. By design, these are intended to be device-level settings. So, you will need to set the desired filters on each KDS. After I update filters, do I need to reboot the device? No, these updates should be reflected immediately. If they are not, try rebooting the POS. Are there permission blocks I can enable for the KDS? No. The KDS is not currently gated by any customizable permissions. How do I change the order sort order? Under Settings, click Order Management. From here, you can choose how orders in your In Progress and Ready tabs are displayed. You can sort orders by Oldest first or Most recent first . You can make different selections for each of these tabs. Can I mark specific items as Ready on a KDS order? Yes. With "item status" on KDS, you can mark individual items within an order as Ready. If you double tap a specific item, that item is marked ready with a green check . The entire order is market ready once all items are marked ready across all KDS views. I accidentally marked an item as ready. Can I undo it? No. Once an item is marked as Ready, that item cannot be unchecked. 🧰 Troubleshooting If double-tapping doesn’t mark an order Ready: Try tapping again and check that your KDS is connected to the network. If KDS loses internet mid-rush: Orders from POS continue flowing via LAN (Note: a functioning Local Area Network or LAN is a requirement for the KDS order flow to continue uninterrupted during brief loss of internet. Resetting or restarting the POS may interrupt this, as well). Online or Marketplace orders will resume once connection is restored. In this case, you will see a red status bar appear on the KDS. This status bar indicates the connection status between the POS and the KDS. Red = Disconnected Black = Connected Because these devices are connected via Ethernet, there are a few requirements to ensure that the devices can "see" and communicate with each other. The devices are ethernet connected and must be on the same network, so you will first ensure that all devices (POS and KDS) are connected to the same switch and/or router. To note, they don't necessarily need to be connected to the same switch, but any peripheral devices (like a switch), need to trace back to the same source of internet (eg, router). To confirm, you may need to physically trace the cables back to their source. Next, ensure that ports on both ends of your device are securely connected. A physical connection is confirmed by a light appearing on the port. This light may be solid or blinking, but if you do not see a light, you may need to attempt a different port, or replace the cable. Assuming a functioning physical connection, you need to confirm there is data passing betwene the devices. You would expect to see blinking link lights on both ends of the Ethernet ports to indicate the devices are successfully transmitting data. If you run into issues, you should try different ports on the device your KDS and POS are connected to (typically a switch or a router), replace the cable to rule out a faulty cable, and ensure you have a functioning ethernet connection. Can duplicate tickets appear? Only if a saved order is updated — new items will appear as new cards under the same ID. Duplicate items will not appear. Why did my ticket turn yellow or red? Color indicates elapsed time since order creation: Yellow: running behind (~10 minutes) Red: late (~15 minutes) Why do orders disappear overnight? KDS automatically clears completed orders at the end of each day. If an item doesn’t appear on KDS: Check if that item is assigned to a prep station linked to the KDS. Items not mapped to a prep station won’t display on KDS, but still appear in LOM. It also may be filtered out by item category, channel, or fulfillment type on the KDS itself. KDS Showing “Not Connected” Despite Other Hardware Online ✔️ Step 1 — Confirm the basics Ensure all other devices (POS, printers, kiosk) are online Power-cycle the KDS Open POS → Settings → Connected Devices. If the KDS appears but shows “Not Connected,” continue below. ✔️ Step 2 — Check the physical cable (if applicable) Verify the ethernet/network cable is securely connected. A loose cable can prevent the KDS from negotiating a connection. If cables are secure and no change occurs → continue. ✔️ Step 3 — Check the Comm Server Status If the POS → Settings → Connected Devices screen shows: Server Status: Stopped Connected Server: not connected to server then the Comm Server needs to be restarted. ✔️ Step 4 — Resolution: Press “Restart” on the Comm Server Screen From the same screen, tap Restart . This restarts the internal communication service. Within ~10 seconds, the following should update: Server Status → Running Connected Server → Connected KDS should reconnect automatically Other Troubleshooting Questions What if there are items missing from my order? Check the filtering view to understand which item categories are currently being shown. Next, check the Merchant Portal to understand the configuration of your item categories. If you have similar items in different categories, you may be accidentally filtering out items you don't intend to. Duplicate tickets appear to be flowing through the KDS. How is this happening? You should never see duplicate tickets on your KDS. The only exception is when new items are added to Saved Orders. In this case, these will be displayed as a new order card with a matching Order ID, but they should not show duplicative items. 💻 Hardware & Setup What hardware is used for KDS? KDS runs on a durable 15" Elo Android touchscreen. Can it be mounted? Yes. The device supports wall, counter, or stand mounting. Does it have speakers? Yes, though sound alerts are not yet available. Does KDS require its own internet connection? No. It connects via Wi-Fi or Ethernet on the same network as your POS. If multiple POS are connected: Orders and status updates automatically sync across all POS terminals and your KDS. 🏁 Summary The KDS provides a centralized, digital view of all active orders so your kitchen can work more efficiently. Orders appear automatically from all connected channels. You can mark orders Ready directly from the screen. The KDS continues to function offline for POS orders. Completed orders stay visible in the Ready tab until the end of day. If you experience any syncing issues, missing orders, or device errors, contact your support team for help verifying connectivity and confirming that your items are mapped correctly to prep stations.

articles.body: You can follow these steps to connect your scanner: Lift the merchant-facing screen: The screen swivels up and down. Gently swivel it upward to access the area underneath. Locate and remove the panel: Beneath the screen, you’ll see a panel. Use a screwdriver to remove the screws securing the panel: Find the USB ports: Once the panel is removed, you’ll see a set of USB ports. Connect the scanner: Plug your scanner cable into one of the available USB ports Run the cable through the opening: There’s a small opening at the bottom of the panel area. You can feed the scanner cable through this opening to keep your setup tidy: Reattach the panel. Once the cable is in place, screw the panel back on.Swivel the screen back down to its normal position. Your scanner should now be connected and ready to use!

articles.body: To allow customers to buy gift cards online and redeem them in-store or through DoorDash online ordering, you’ll need to set up a Stripe account. Stripe will securely process the payments, and eCard Systems will create a custom gift card landing page for your business. Stripe Setup Guide for Gift Cards Stripe is quick to set up and easy to use with simple pay-as-you-go pricing. You can set up a new Stripe account here: https://dashboard.stripe.com/register . Please follow Stripe's instructions on Creating Account & Connecting to Bank. Once done: Share Developer access with jon.stripe@netmasons.com More information on Managing Access to your Organization can be found here: Navigate to the Team page Click Add Member Add the email address of the user you want to invite: jon.stripe@netmasons.com Under User Roles , select “Developer” Select the account(s) that you want to give this user access to. You can select individual accounts, or grant access to the entire organization. Org-level access will give users access to all accounts within the organization, as well as access to the organization itself. Click Send Invites to send the email with the steps for creating their Stripe Account Make sure to verify your phone as the account holder Setup 2FA (Two-Factor Authentication) via Stripe.

articles.title: Gift Card Reporting
articles.snippet: Overview: This article provides a summary of the tools available to hep you track and manage gift card activity. You can access reports on gift card sales, redemptions and other financial details through Point of Sale Reports and the ECS Reports Portal. eCS Reports Portal: As part of your gift card
articles.body: Overview: This article provides a summary of the tools available to hep you track and manage gift card activity. You can access reports on gift card sales, redemptions and other financial details through Point of Sale Reports and the ECS Reports Portal. eCS Reports Portal: As part of your gift card setup, you should have received login credentials for the eCS Reports Portal from eCard Systems during onboarding. If you haven't received your login details or need access again, please contact our support team. The eCS Reports Portal provides additional reporting to help you track gift card activity in more detail. Some of the most commonly used reports include: Transaction Detail Reports: gives a summary or detailed breakdown of all gift card transaction types, such as card loads and redemptions. You can view data by merchant, location or terminal for added flexibility Single Card History Reports: shows the full transaction history for an individual gift card. It's useful if a customer has questions about their card balance, you can use this report to verify their activity Pooling Reports: if your business uses a pooling setup, eCS will email a summary report each month. This will show an overview of how funds are distributed across locations DoorDash Reports: In addition to the ECS reports, DoorDash also provides built-in reporting tools to help you track and understand gift card activity. These reports are available in two main places: via Your POS: You can view gift card reports from the POS device by navigating to the Reports section via Merchant Portal: Additional reporting is available in the online merchant portal, where you can view gift card data Each platform provides different levels of details to help you manage and reconcile gift card transactions in the sections below, we'll break down what reports are available and how to access them in each location Point of Sale Reports: Cash Out Report: Any cash outs done will appear in the cash drawer activity including the date/time of cash out, employee who performed it and the amount it was for: Merchant Portal: Transactions and Payouts Reports: Gift card sales will show up in this report. Orders that are paid with gift card will show as an adjustment. Refunds on orders that were made by a gift card will show in the 'Error charges&refunds' column On-terminal Gift Card Reporting Guide & Troubleshooting When someone buys a gift card Imagine a customer hands you $100 cash and says, “Give me a gift card.” You now have $100 in your cash register . That $100 shows up in your sales report as a cash sale (or card sale if they paid by card). At this point: you’ve collected money, but the customer hasn’t actually gotten food yet — they just have credit sitting on a card. 2. Gift Card Redemptions When a customer spends their gift card, the reporting shows two things: The redemption value ($100) is added to Cash Sales (because a gift card is treated like cash when used). That same $100 is shown as a negative line (to cancel it out, so you don’t double-count). Why this matters If the system didn’t do this, it would look like you made: $100 when the card was bought, plus another $100 when it was spent, … which would make it seem like you earned $200 when in reality you only earned $100. The “adjustment” (negative line) fixes this so your revenue isn’t double counted . Now, depending on the report, this negative line is labeled differently: In-Store Sales Tab → Shows as a line called “Redemptions.” Financials Tab → Shows as “Redemptions” as well, using the same logic to avoid double counting. Gift Cards Tab → Shows the number and dollar value of redemptions directly, separate from purchases. 👉 Everywhere above, the word “Redemptions” is used. 3. Merchant Portal Here’s where it’s different: In the Merchant Portal, purchases are counted as revenue. Redemptions do not appear as “redemptions.” Instead, they show up under the line item “Adjustments.” This is just a labeling difference. It’s the same mechanic (subtracting redemptions so you don’t count the money twice), but here the system groups them with adjustments. 4. Employee Sales Tab Purchases: Count as cash or card sales depending on payment method. Redemptions: Count as cash sales . 👉 Here they’re simply rolled into sales totals, not labeled as adjustment Report / Tab Gift Card Purchase Gift Card Redemption How It’s Labeled In-Store Sales Counts as Cash Sales (if paid in cash) or Card Sales (if paid by card) Shows as Cash Sales , and the same amount shows as a negative on Redemptions line Redemptions Financials Same as above Same as above Redemptions Employee Sales Counts toward employee’s sales (as Cash or Card, depending on purchase method) Counts toward employee’s sales as Cash Sales Rolled into sales totals (not labeled “Adjustment”) Gift Cards Tab Shows total number of gift cards purchased and total revenue Shows total number and dollar amount of redemptions Redemptions Merchant Portal (online) Purchases count as Revenue Redemptions show as a negative line under Adjustments Adjustments

articles.body: Overview This article provides a guide on using gift cards with your point of sale systems. It covers the different type of gift card transactions, including selling, redeeming and more. Loading an Re-Loading a Gift Card 1. Start sale and POS and build cart 2. Add gift card item. Currently we do not support the sale of gift cards and other items. Gift card sales will need to be processed as a separate sale from other items the customer is planning to purchase. 3. Manually enter the gift card number on the back of the card or scan the barcode to bring up the card number. 4. Select a predefined or custom amount that will be loaded onto the card. We support a load amount from $10 - $500. 5. Select Add to Order and proceed to checkout screen for payment 5. Finish Sale. Redeeming a Gift Card NOTE: Split payments using gift card and cash are not currently supported. We do support split payments using gift card and credit/debit card, but only one card can be used per transaction and the gift card must be redeemed in full first. 1. Start sale on POS and build the cart. 2. Select Checkout. 3. Select Apply gift card. 4. Scan or enter gift card number first . If the balance does not cover the total order amount, customer will be prompted to enter credit or debit card for the remaining balance 5. Finish sale Refunding Gift Card Payments 1. Navigate to Order History 2. Select Order that requires refund 3. Select Issue Refund on the top right of the screen 4. If the order was paid in full by gift card, select the items that will be refunded and proceed by selecting Send Refund. If the order was paid partially by gift card, you will see a breakdown of the refund amounts and which payment methods they will be going to. Please note we do not currently support partial refunds for gift cards, so if the order was fully or partially paid by a gift card, the full order will be refunded to the respective cards 5. Select Refund Cash Outs In certain states, local laws require that customers can "cash out" a remaining balance on a gift card. This means the customer can request to receive the remaining funds in cash instead of spending them in store. How does it Work? We currently support gift card cash outs for balanced between $0 and $20. If a customer requests a cash out and their balance qualifies, you'll see a cash out button on the gift card screen on the POS. Tap cash out and provide the remaining balance to the customer. Balance Checks Customers can check their balance online through eCS' balance checker . When a customer pays with a gift card, the remaining balance will also be printed on their receipt. You can always view the current balance on the gift card screen on your POS.

articles.snippet: How can I purchase physical gift cards? You can head to our card order page to order either generic or custom cards. articles.body: How can I purchase physical gift cards? You can head to our card order page to order either generic or custom cards. Generic card orders have a processing time of 3-5 days for generic cards and up to 14 days for custom cards. For any additional questions regarding gift card orders, you can also contact eCS directly at 1-866-776-7409, and choose Ext. 1. How can I sell digital/e-gift cards? eCS can build and host a unique landing page for your store. This page allows customers to conveniently purchase digital cards online. Once your page is ready, you can add the link to your website to promote online gift card sales. Before eCS can create your landing page, there are a few setup steps you'll need to complete. Please follow the instructions in the digital gift card setup guide to make sure everything is ready. If you need any assistance, reach out to our support team! How can a I re-order gift cards? Head over to our card order page to place a re-order. For any additional questions regarding gift card orders, you can also contact eCS directly at 1-866-776-7409, and choose Ext. 1. How can I view my reports? DoorDash does offer some gift card reporting, but for more granular reports, you can also use eCS' reports portal . You will be given login credentials during your gift card onboarding but if you ever need help accessing your account again, feel free to reach out to our support team. Can customers check their balance? Customers can check their balance online through eCS' balance checker When a customer pays with a gift card, the remaining balance will also be printed on the receipt. How will I be billed? You will be billed directly from eCS for the gift card program and any card orders placed. If there are any billing related concerns, you can speak with eCS to resolve them. They can be contacted at support at 1-866-776-7409, and choose Ext. 3 or emailing doordashsupport@ecardsystems.com .

articles.title: Gift Cards: Obtaining your Conversion Reports
articles.snippet: Overview If you're migrating a gift card program to eCard Systems for use with your DoorDash POS, this guide explains the required conversion report data. Providing the correct report ensures all balances transfer seamlessly, allowing your customers to continue using their gift cards. What You Need
articles.body: Overview If you're migrating a gift card program to eCard Systems for use with your DoorDash POS, this guide explains the required conversion report data. Providing the correct report ensures all balances transfer seamlessly, allowing your customers to continue using their gift cards. What You Need to Provide eCS requires Conversion Reports from your current gift card provider so that they can convert the existing balances over. You should be able to pull these reports directly from your POS/Gift Card Provider but if not, reach out to their support team for help. Note: Please allow enough time to obtain the correct gift card liability report as it may take up to several days. Once the report is generated, refrain from processing any further gift card transactions. The report should be an unedited gift card balance report including: Date Range from Present to 2+ years back Gift card numbers on the report should match the ones on the physical gift cards Should contain every gift card sold and the current balance Should also include all $0 balance gift cards and unsold cards. If a report cannot be obtained for this, you may need to provide a file of the card numbers manually Provider Timeline Fees Associated Additional Info Aloha Days ⚠️ May apply Called 'Aloha Stored Value Liability by Date Range' This should include unsold cards but if it doesn't, please request for it. Clover Days ✅ Covered by Us Fiserv Days ✅ Covered by Us Does not provide an unused list Heartland Days ✅ Covered by Us The liability report does not typically include unsold card numbers and Heartland does not provide this Mx will need to contact GC printing company or manually provide excel/csv of card numbers Example Paytronix Days ✅ Covered by Us Shift4/Customer Connection Days ⚠️ May apply Usually, report will include the unsold cards If not, ECS requires an excel or csv of those card numbers *May charge for the final unmasked file Example Square Days ✅ Covered by Us Mx should ask for “Final Card Balance” that includes full card numbers and balances (including cents) Example Toast Days ✅ Covered by Us Valutec 24-48 Hr ⚠️ May apply Separate file for their unsold gift cards Need to request an inactive file/unmasked liability. * May charge for the final unmasked file Worldpay 24-48 Hr ⚠️ May apply Separate file for their unsold gift cards Need to request an inactive file/unmasked liability. * May charge for the final unmasked file Submitting Your Report If you have the report when signing your Pathfinder and eCS agreements, you can share it directly with your onboarding rep. They will submit it to eCS on your behalf and you should be available via phone/email for any follow up questions. eCS does not process conversions after 12 p.m. Friday, on Holidays or over the weekend.

We can be reached by text at 1-574-475-3274 or support@doordash-instore.zendesk.com When reaching out to our team, videos showing a suspected bug or unexpected behavior are extremely helpful in our investigation. articles.title: Remote M2 Card Reader Swap Instructions
articles.snippet: We are working to roll out a new version card reader to merchants who are experiencing card reader connectivity issues. The POS Support team will reach out to you proactively if you are identified as being a good candidate for this new card reader and assist you with the steps below. Preparing For I
articles.body: We are working to roll out a new version card reader to merchants who are experiencing card reader connectivity issues. The POS Support team will reach out to you proactively if you are identified as being a good candidate for this new card reader and assist you with the steps below. Preparing For Installation Ensure you reach out to POS Support prior to following these steps as they will need to configure settings on the back-end to ensure your new card reader connects properly. POS Support will need the serial number from your card reader as well as the device id for your POS . The serial number for the card reader can be found on the back of the reader as shown here The device id for your POS can be found by navigating to settings and scrolling to the bottom Connecting your New Card Reader DO NOT proceed to these steps until POS Support has confirmed it is okay to move forward with the installation after providing them with the information above. Disconnect the old card reader from the POS and network by unplugging all cords connected to the reader and powering it off Remove the front plate from the POS which is located directly under the screen. Note: Depending on your POS model you may need a screwdriver to remove the front plate. If you do not have a screwdriver and require assistance please notify POS support. Plug in the USB cord for the new card reader into any available blue USB-A port on the POS. Connect the other end of the USB cord to the new card reader. Once the new reader is fully connected you should see a “Card Reader/Firmware Updating” message on your status bar at the top of your POS. Allow this update to complete before performing any actions on the POS. Once the update is complete the “Card Reader/Firmware Updating” messaging will no longer show in the status bar of your POS and your new card reader is now ready to use! **We suggest running a test transaction if possible to ensure operation.

articles.body: DoorDash Kiosk's include an optional feature to collect customer names during checkout — helping you streamline food handoff and improve order coordination. Collect Customer Names at Checkout When this feature is turned on , customers will be prompted to enter their name before completing their order at the kiosk. The name entered will then appear on all kitchen tickets , along with the ticket number. This helps your staff match orders to customers faster and improve accuracy during handoff. How to Turn It On or Off: This feature is off by default but can be toggled easily from your kiosk. To enable or disable: On the kiosk, swipe left to right from the left side the screen Enter your employee code Tap Settings Toggle the "Collect customer name" option on or off

articles.title: Live Orders Tab
articles.snippet: We’re excited to share a new update to your DoorDash POS: the Live Orders tab . This feature helps you view and manage all your orders in one place — including DoorDash Marketplace, Online Ordering, and POS orders. You’ll now have more visibility, better tracking, and easier control over your orders
articles.body: We’re excited to share a new update to your DoorDash POS: the Live Orders tab . This feature helps you view and manage all your orders in one place — including DoorDash Marketplace, Online Ordering, and POS orders. You’ll now have more visibility, better tracking, and easier control over your orders. What’s New View All Orders in One Tab The Live Orders tab shows: DoorDash Marketplace orders Online Ordering orders In-store POS orders You no longer need to switch between systems to track different order types. Saved/Scheduled Orders Saved or scheduled orders will now automatically show up in the Live Orders tab when they’re placed. Manual Order Confirmation (If Applicable) Some stores will now be asked to manually confirm orders before preparing them. If you see a "Confirm order" button, simply tap to confirm and begin prep. Orders Sync Across All Terminals If your store uses more than one POS terminal, any actions (like marking an order as ready) will now show on all devices automatically. Fulfillment Type Is Clearly Labeled Each order shows where it came from (DoorDash, Online Ordering, or POS), so you can prioritize accordingly. Interacting with Orders In order to change the order stage, just click the dialog at the bottom of the order card. For example, click "Ready for Pickup" when the order is ready to be picked up by a Dasher or passed along to an in-store customer. This will move it from the In progress tab to the Ready tab. Once an order has been picked up or handed to your customer, hit "Mark Picked up" to clear it from your Ready tab. Status Bar Notifications (Top of POS) You’ll now see updates like: Order confirmed Dasher arriving New scheduled order Order canceled Orders need action Note: These updates are informational only — they can’t be clicked or tapped. Order Details Are Now More Interactive Tap into any order to see: Full item details Pickup time or delivery info Customer name Dasher status (if applicable) Reprint the ticket (by clicking the printer icon seen in the lower lefthand corner of the order, Screenshot Below ) See below for accessing the reprint button for a ticket: Printing Your POS printers can be configured to automatically print DoorDash Marketplace tickets, along with your other ticket types Navigate to the Merchant Portal > Point of Sale > Kitchen Locate the printer you wish to print from. Click the pencil icon to make any adjustments. Set DoorDash receipts = 1 (or however many you would like), scroll to the bottom, and click Update Printer . If you do not click this button, changes will not save. Then, on the Point of Sale terminal, Navigate to Settings > Click "Refresh Menus & Printer Connections" If orders do not print automatically, you can manually reprint from the order card in the Live Orders tab (see section above for details). Critical note: Marketplace tablets can only connect via Bluetooth to dedicated Marketplace printers. Attempting to Bluetooth-connect the Marketplace tablet directly to your POS printers will disrupt all printing. So, f you want Marketplace orders to print on your POS printers, this must be configured in the Kitchen tab of your Merchant Portal, as outlined in this section. Filtering Live Orders Filters let you control what appears on the Live Orders tab by: Channel: DoorDash, Online Ordering, POS, Kiosk, UberEats Fulfillment Type: Dine-in, Takeout, Delivery, Pickup, Drive-Thru, Curbside, Catering, or Phone You can combine filters (for example, “POS + Drive-Thru”) to narrow your view to specific types of orders. This helps reduce clutter on the Live Orders screen and improves accuracy when managing orders in high-volume environments. Learn more about filtering here: Filtering the Live Orders Tab on the POS What to Expect You do not need to take any action to enable this feature. It will appear automatically on your POS. Keep your DoorDash tablet nearby for now. Some features (like contacting the Dasher or issuing refunds) are still only available on the tablet. Kiosk orders are not yet supported in the Live Orders tab. We’re working to include them soon. There are some features that we don't support today that will require you to retain your DoorDash tablet (for now!). Here is a list of the actions that we hope to support soon: Pause Store Contact Dasher Cancel Order Dasher Rating Contact DoorDash (Marketplace) Customer Contact Online Ordering Customer Refund Order Scheduled order adjustments Notification sounds from the POS

articles.title: Fulfillment Types in DoorDash POS
articles.snippet: Overview The DoorDash POS now allows you to select and configure Fulfillment Types directly in the cart. This feature improves operational clarity, speeds up checkout, and ensures that both staff and customers are aligned on how orders should be handled — whether they’re for dine-in, takeout, pickup
articles.body: Overview The DoorDash POS now allows you to select and configure Fulfillment Types directly in the cart. This feature improves operational clarity, speeds up checkout, and ensures that both staff and customers are aligned on how orders should be handled — whether they’re for dine-in, takeout, pickup, or delivery. Check out this quick demo video (Password: DDPOS2025) Benefits of Fulfillment Types Faster Checkout – Set a default fulfillment type (e.g., "Pickup") so it's pre-selected for every order. Clearer Tickets & Receipts – The selected fulfillment type prints on both kitchen tickets and customer receipts. Customizable Settings – Easily toggle on/off fulfillment types, reorder them, and choose a default. A ctionable Insights – View fulfillment-based sales breakdowns in the Merchant Portal > Sales tab. How to Select a Fulfillment Type During Checkout From the Checkout screen , build the order as usual. In the top-right corner of the order summary panel, you’ll now see fulfillment type options: For Here , To Go , Pickup , Delivery , and others (if enabled). Tap to select the appropriate fulfillment type before checking out. How to Configure Fulfillment Types in POS Settings Tap Settings in the bottom navigation bar. Go to Fulfillment Types . From this screen, you can: Enable or disable fulfillment types (toggle switch). Rearrange order using drag-and-drop. Set your default by moving the desired option to the top spot. Supported fulfillment types include: For Here To Go Pickup Delivery Drive-Thru Curbside Catering Phone How Fulfillment Types Appear on Tickets and Receipts Once selected, the fulfillment type appears clearly on printed order tickets and receipts. This helps kitchen staff and front-of-house teams know how to handle each order: View Fulfillment Data in Merchant Portal You can track sales performance by fulfillment method directly in the Merchant Portal: Go to the Merchant Portal Navigate to Insights > Sales Use the Fulfillment Method filter to view performance by channel Important Notes Only one fulfillment type can be assigned per order. Fulfillment Types : not editable, but default is configurable and order they appear is configurable. You cannot add custom items Revenue Centers are still supported for workflows that require them. To access them, tap the ••• menu on the top-right of the cart. Revenue Centers: totally configurable, you can call these whatever you want. The button for Revenue Centers is gone, but you can still access them. If you add a revenue center and a fulfillment type, only the Fulfillment Type will print on the ticket/receipt. We cannot edit this. You cannot turn off fulfillment types. You need at least one active in your Fulfillment Type Settings.

articles.title: Checking Out an Order
articles.snippet: When you’ve finished adding items to an order, tap the Checkout button in the bottom-right corner of the screen. You’ll also have the option to: Enter a customer name Add order notes (e.g., delivery address, “prepare for dine-in,” “pick-up,” etc.) 👉 Note: This pop-up screen can be disabled in the Se
articles.body: When you’ve finished adding items to an order, tap the Checkout button in the bottom-right corner of the screen. You’ll also have the option to: Enter a customer name Add order notes (e.g., delivery address, “prepare for dine-in,” “pick-up,” etc.) 👉 Note: This pop-up screen can be disabled in the Settings section of your POS. After hitting Check out and entering the customer information and notes, the experience will change based on the (1) payment type, (2) whether you have a customer-facing display, and (3) whether you have tipping enabled. Credit Card: If you have tipping configured, customers will be prompted to select a tip. You can skip this screen on the POS tablet, as well. The screen below shows what your customers will see on the customer-facing display. If you do not have a customer-facing display on your POS, but have tipping configured, the customer will be prompted to add a tip directly on the payment reader . Manual Credit Card: If you are manually entering card details (eg, a phone order), you will add any tip on your end. Cash: For a cash order, you will be prompted to select the amount tendered from a preset list of options, or by entering a custom amount. In all cases, the payment screen will default to preparing an order now, but you also have the option to Schedule Ahead . For more information on Scheduled Orders, check out the article here .

articles.snippet: Adding Items to an Order Just a quick NOTE to begin: you can always make sure your menu is up-to-date by pressing the refresh button at the top left Tapping on an item will add it to the order. If there are required item modifiers, you will automatically be shown the modifier choices you need to sel
articles.body: Adding Items to an Order Just a quick NOTE to begin: you can always make sure your menu is up-to-date by pressing the refresh button at the top left Tapping on an item will add it to the order. If there are required item modifiers, you will automatically be shown the modifier choices you need to select An item with no required modifiers will be directly added to the order pane on the right. If you want to add special instructions or select optional modifier choices, you can tap on the item in the right hand pane to bring up the modifier screen Adding Open Items With Customer Pricing If created, there will be a menu category called “Open Item” that contains items with open pricing. This category can be moved up or down in any order desired through the Merchant Portal. Once you select this item, you will need to enter the price you want to charge. Optionally, you can also enter an item name and item description for the receipt and kitchen ticket. You can have multiple open item buttons for different item tax configurations. You can learn more about how to configure your open item buttons in the Open item management section of the guide Open Item Management You can have multiple Open Item buttons in your POS. If you would like to create or adjust these open item buttons, please contact your DoorDash implementation specialist or account manager, and we’ll change it for you. For each open item button, you’ll need to specify the following: Name of button Item tax rate (if none specified, we will default to the store tax rate set in your DoorDash Merchant Portal settings)

articles.body: Discount and Surcharges Configuration To customize the types of discount/surcharge buttons that show up in your POS system, go to the DoorDash Merchant Portal ( doordash.com/merchant ) and navigate to Point of Sale > Discounts & Surcharges . For each entry, you can specify the following settings: Name of button (with description). For example, a name may be "10% off" or "Happy hour discount" Note: the description will not show on the POS, so include any details you need viewable in the discount name (Eg, Happy Hour 10% off) Set as either a discount (money off) or surcharge (additional charge) Set as either percentage-based or fixed-fee-based Percentage based: 20% off, 4% surcharge Fixed-fee: $5 off, +$3.00 surcharge Automatic Surcharge: When you add a percentage based surcharge, there is a toggle below the amount that will allow you to set this as an automatic surcharge . This will automatically be added to any credit card transactions. You can only have a single surcharge set as automatic. Updating a Surcharge or Discount To edit/update a surcharge or discount, simply click on the item you wish to edit in the Merchant Portal . Currently only name and description can be updated. If you want to change the type, amount or auto vs. manual surcharge, please deactivate the item and create a new one. Note: Any discount/surcharge is applied to the entire order. Surcharges do not apply to gift card transactions, partial payment, or debit cards. This tool is only for creating discounts and surcharges applicable to DoorDash POS Orders. This will not be usable, visible or available for any other channel (Marketplace, Online Ordering, etc). For more information on Auto Surcharges, check it out here: Automatic Credit Card Surcharges on POS If you don't have a customer-facing display (dual screen), refer to this article for instructions: Enabling Auto Credit Card Surcharges (No Customer Facing Display/Dual Screen)

articles.body: When creating an order, you can chose to save an order and take payment at a later time (e.g., when processing phone orders). To do so, press the Save button at the top right of the order entry screen. On the modal that pops up, you will need to enter a Customer Name. Optionally, you can add to the Additional Notes field By default, the Print Ticket option will be checked, meaning that a kitchen ticket will get printed when the order is saved. You can uncheck this option if you’d like to only print the kitchen ticket upon checkout Viewing a Saved Order & Checking it Out You can also view your saved orders by opening up the hamburger menu ( ☰ ) at the top left of the POS screen and then tapping on the Saved Orders tab From the Saved Orders screen, you can tap on any saved order, which will then populate it in the order entry flow for you to check out. You can also reprint kitchen tickets from that screen NOTE: Once you save an order, the items in the basket cannot be edited, however specific items can still be removed. If you incorrectly added an item and need to edit it, you'll need to remove the item and then add the item back to the basket to edit the modifiers or other options.

Steps to Take a Phone Payment on the POS: Create the Order Build the order on your POS just like you would fo
articles.body: If a customer is placing an order over the phone — such as for party trays or catering — and you'd like to take their credit card payment in advance, you can do so directly through your POS. Steps to Take a Phone Payment on the POS: Create the Order Build the order on your POS just like you would for any other in-store order. Click "Check Out" Add the Customer's Name This helps you track and reference the order later if needed. (You will need to have the Skip Additional Info Prompt toggled off within the POS Settings for this) Choose "Manual Credit Card Entry" On the left-hand side of the checkout screen, you'll see the option for Manual Credit Card Entry . Select this to enter the customer's card details while you're on the phone. Optional: Save the Order First If you're not ready to run the payment right away (for example, if the customer is paying in person later): Click "Save Order" instead of checking out. Go to Saved Orders along the bottom of your POS screen From here, you can select the order when you're ready. Once selected you can either: Manually enter the card, or Use the card reader if the customer is now in-store.

articles.title: Filtering the Live Orders Tab on the POS
articles.snippet: Overview The Live Orders tab in Pathfinder POS shows every active order across all connected sales channels — DoorDash, Online Ordering, UberEats, Kiosk, and in-store POS. With Live Orders Filters , you can choose which orders appear on the screen, helping your team focus on what matters most for th
articles.body: Overview The Live Orders tab in Pathfinder POS shows every active order across all connected sales channels — DoorDash, Online Ordering, UberEats, Kiosk, and in-store POS. With Live Orders Filters , you can choose which orders appear on the screen, helping your team focus on what matters most for their role or station. 🔎 What This Feature Does Live Orders Filters let you control what appears on the Live Orders tab by: Channel: DoorDash, Online Ordering, POS, Kiosk, UberEats Fulfillment Type: Dine-in, Takeout, Delivery, Pickup, Drive-Thru, Curbside, Catering, or Phone You can combine filters (for example, “POS + Drive-Thru”) to narrow your view to specific types of orders. This helps reduce clutter on the Live Orders screen and improves accuracy when managing orders in high-volume environments. Example: Drive-Thru POS shows only Drive-Thru orders. Expo Station shows only Pickup and Delivery. Front Counter POS shows only dine-in and takeout. ⚙️ How to Use Live Orders Filters 1. Open the Live Orders Tab From the POS home screen, tap Live Orders to view all active orders. 2. Tap the Filter Icon In the top-right corner, tap the filter icon to open your filtering options. 3. Choose Your Filters Select one or more filters: By Channel – DoorDash, Online Ordering, POS, Kiosk, UberEats By Fulfillment Type – Dine-in, Takeout, Delivery, Pickup, Drive-Thru, and more You can apply both types together (for example, “Online Ordering + Delivery”). 4. Apply Filters Tap Apply . The screen will refresh instantly, showing only orders that match your selections. Filtering is visual only — all orders continue to sync in the background and route correctly to printers, KDS screens, and prep stations. 5. Clear Filters To show all orders again, tap the filter icon and select Clear All . 💡 Key Details Filters are device-specific. Each POS maintains its own settings. Changing filters on one device doesn’t affect others. Filters persist automatically. Once set, they remain applied until you change or clear them — even if you log out. Filters can’t be set in the Merchant Portal. They can only be configured directly on the POS. Works offline. Filtering doesn’t require a network connection; you can continue using filters in offline mode. Instant updates. When you adjust filters, your Live Orders screen updates immediately without interrupting order sync. No performance impact. Filtering doesn’t slow your device or delay new orders — hidden orders still sync normally. 🧩 Notifications & Manual Confirmation Notifications follow your filters. If you’ve hidden certain order types, you won’t receive alerts for those orders until they’re visible again. Manual confirmation orders: If your store uses manual confirmation for Marketplace (MP) orders and you’ve filtered out MP channels, those orders will not appear on the POS. You’ll need to confirm them directly from your DoorDash tablet. 🧭 Troubleshooting Don’t see the filter icon? Make sure your POS app version is 1.174.x or higher . Restart your device. If the icon is still missing, contact Support — the feature may not yet be enabled for your store. Can’t find an order after filtering? Clear or adjust your filters to Show All Orders — the order will reappear immediately. Order notifications don’t match what you see on-screen? That’s expected when filters are active; notifications only trigger for visible order types. Filters reset unexpectedly? Filters are saved per device. If a device was replaced or reset, filters will need to be re-applied. 📈 Use Cases Simplify high-volume screens: Reduce clutter by hiding channels that your staff doesn’t manage directly. Specialize by station: Use filters to create focused views for different roles (Drive-Thru, Expo, Front Counter). Reduce tablet dependency: Many stores now manage all online channels (DoorDash, Online Ordering, UberEats) directly from the Live Orders tab. Support scheduled orders: Scheduled orders appear automatically if their channel and fulfillment type match your current filters. 📞 Need Help? Check your POS version under Settings → About at the bottom of the screen. If your app version is below 1.174.x , text Support at 1-888-789-7099 to request an update, or simply leave your POS powered on overnight for automatic updates.

articles.title: Item Level Ticket Printing
articles.snippet: We now support item level ticket printing . This feature, if configured in your Merchant Portal, will allow you to print individual tickets for specific items on an order. To enable this feature, you will need to update your printer settings for the printer(s) you want to support this type of ticket
articles.body: We now support item level ticket printing . This feature, if configured in your Merchant Portal, will allow you to print individual tickets for specific items on an order. To enable this feature, you will need to update your printer settings for the printer(s) you want to support this type of ticket printing. To do this: 1. Navigate to the Kitchen section of the Merchant Portal (under the Point of Sale tab) 2. Click the pen icon to edit the printer settings. 3. To support item-level tickets, you will need to update the field called # of single-item tickets to be a number greater than “0”. For example, If you set this to “1” that means any item you configure to print on their own ticket will print a single item-level ticket in addition to the main ticket for the order. 4. From there, you will then need to select which items on your menu you want to print item-level tickets by navigating to the Kitchen section of the Merchant Portal (under the Point of Sale tab) and editing your Prep Station (s). In the below example, this merchant has bagels, sandwiches, and hot drinks all routed to the printer associated with this prep station (indicated by the check mark on the left), but only Breakfast Burrito 18 and all hot drinks set to print item-level tickets (indicated by the check mark on the right). For items that are set to print item-level tickets, those item-level tickets will indicate that the item is part of a larger order (eg “partial order: 1 of 4 items”). All items will still show up on the primary kitchen ticket, regardless of whether they are printed at the item-level or not. Lastly, you will notice that the prep station screen has a slightly updated look and feel. articles.title: Sequential Ticket Numbers Across POS & Kiosks
articles.snippet: Overview If you use more than one POS and/or kiosk, ticket numbers will now count up in one shared sequence across all devices . Before this update, each device could generate its own ticket sequence. That meant two different orders could both show the same ticket number (for example, “#102” on a PO
articles.body: Overview If you use more than one POS and/or kiosk, ticket numbers will now count up in one shared sequence across all devices . Before this update, each device could generate its own ticket sequence. That meant two different orders could both show the same ticket number (for example, “#102” on a POS and “#102” on a kiosk), which caused confusion during prep and handoff. With sequential ticket numbers enabled, every order—no matter where it’s placed—gets a unique ticket number in the same sequence. What you’ll see Ticket numbers will increment across devices in the order they’re received. Example: POS order: #102 Kiosk order: #103 POS order: #104 Kiosk order: #105 So you may see ticket numbers “alternating” between POS and kiosks depending on order flow—and that’s expected. Who is impacted All merchants will receive this update. The biggest change will be for merchants using multiple POS devices and/or kiosks , since those setups were most likely to see duplicate ticket numbers previously. Do I need to do anything? No. This update turns on automatically. Can I configure ticket numbering by device? No. Once this is live: You can’t set each POS/kiosk to start at different ticket numbers (ex: POS 1 starts at 100, POS 2 starts at 200). All devices contribute to one shared ticket number sequence , starting from 100 and counting up. Does this work with… Saved orders? Yes. Kiosks? Yes. Offline mode? Yes— as long as all devices are on the same network . Requirements To use sequential ticket numbering, your setup must meet these basics: All POS/kiosk devices are on the same network Devices are running software version 1.189.x or newer (If you don’t know your version, Support can help confirm.) Troubleshooting Ticket numbers don’t look sequential (or duplicates appear) The most common cause is a temporary local connectivity issue between devices (sometimes called “local comms”). If devices can’t communicate briefly, ticket-number syncing can fail until connectivity recovers. What to expect: This is typically a short interruption (a few minutes) . Merchants can’t fix this from settings —it’s driven by device-to-device connectivity. What you can do: Confirm all devices are still on the same network If the issue persists (not resolving within a few minutes), contact Support Rare edge case: two orders at the exact same moment In an extremely rare scenario where two orders are created at the exact same moment , duplicate ticket numbers may occur. This is considered a theoretical limitation and is expected to be very uncommon.

articles.title: Printer and Prep Station Management
articles.snippet: What is a Prep Station? articles.body: What is a Prep Station? For DoorDash Point of Sale, a prep station is a configuration element within the POS system used to route specific menu items to designated areas of the kitchen for preparation. When you create a prep station, you're grouping together menu items that should be prepared in the same location, such as the grill, salad, or drinks station. Prep stations are not inherently tied to any hardware. To function properly, each prep station must be explicitly linked to a printer where tickets will be printed. This allows orders to be automatically routed to the correct part of the kitchen based on what was ordered. Key points: Prep stations organize where items are prepared. You assign which menu items belong to each prep station. Prep stations must be manually assigned to a printer to output tickets. Getting Started In the Merchant Portal ( doordash.com/merchant ), go to Point of Sale > Kitchen to access the Prep Station and Printer management features Creating a Prep Station To begin creating a Prep Station, tap the Create Prep Station button to start the creation process. You will need to enter a Station Name , and you will need to select which items you want to route to this prep station Important notes: If you select no items for the prep station, that means every item will be mapped to that prep station. If you select only some items, you will need to make sure that other items are assigned to a different prep station, or these items will not print anywhere when they are ordered. If this is your sole prep station, you can check the box "Print all current and future items on this prep station." This will ensure any new items you add to your menu are automatically routed here. Updating a Prep Station Once your prep station is created, you will see that you can make edits at the Category level (Eg, "Burgers"), or the item level (eg, Burgers 1, Burgers 2, Burgers 3, etc). By checking the box next to the category or item, you are assigning it to that particular prep station. Once selected, orders containing that item or category will be routed to that prep station. Any items not checked will not be routed to that prep station. Single-Item Tickets The prep station editor is also where you will find the option to print certain menu categories or menu items on single-item tickets. To learn more about item-level ticket printing, click here . Adding a Printer to a Prep Station Once you create the prep station, you have grouped the items that will be routed to the same place. By adding the printer, you are telling the system where (what printer) those items should print. To add a printer, press the Add Printer button. Below, we'll what needs to be added in each of these fields: Printer Name: Give the printer a name. For example, if you will be assigning this to your Fry Station, consider naming it "Fry Station." If this MAC Address: This is essentially the ID of your printer. To locate the MAC address for your printer, follow these instructions. # of tickets: This is the number of kitchen tickets that will print each time you complete an order. # of receipts: This is the number of customer receipts that will print each time you complete an order. Cash Register Attached – Check this if the printer is connected to a cash drawer. This setting needs to be selected for at least one printer, Device ID – This is only required if you have multiple POS terminals and/ or kiosks servicing customers. To find your Device ID, you will need to go to the POS terminal or kiosk screen, click the Settings, and scroll to the bottom where you will find the Device ID Note regarding Adding/Remove Device IDs from Printers: By removing a device ID from a printer, all tickets and receipts, regardless of the POS where you placed the order, will print at that printer. Adding a device ID tells the printer, "only print receipts or tickets when it comes from a device with this Device ID." Editing an Existing Prep Station To edit the items that are routed to a particular prep station, click the pencil icon next to that prep station. From here, you will see all menus, menu categories and menu items. Simply check (or un-check) to make any changes.

articles.body: If you have a customer-facing display , you can create custom surcharges for credit card purchases in your Merchant Portal. These surcharges will be automatically applied to credit card transactions without any manual steps. 1. Self-Serve Setup in Merchant Portal You can create and manage surcharges on your own within your Merchant Portal. How to set up: Navigate to the Discounts and Surcharges section of the Merchant Portal under the Point of Sale tab on the left-hand side. Click “Add a discount or surcharge.” Enter a name for the surcharge (this will appear on the customer’s receipt). Select “Surcharge” and input the amount (either a flat amount or a %). Toggle on “Apply automatically to credit card transactions.” (Optional) Toggle on “Specify minimum transaction amount” if you only want this to apply to orders over a certain total. Your Stripe reader will automatically detect whether the customer is using a credit card and apply the surcharge accordingly. The surcharge cannot be applied to debit card transactions. Automatic Surcharge Messaging at Checkout If your location has a credit card surcharge enabled , customers will now see a clear message on the customer display screen notifying them at the time of payment. The surcharge will be applied to the pre-tax amount (subtotal). 2. Surcharge Breakdown After Payment Once the transaction is complete, customers will also see a breakdown of the total , including the surcharge amount, before selecting a receipt option. Important Notes and Limitations Surcharges cannot be applied to transactions paid with a debit card . Surcharges will be applied to the pre-tax total ( Subtotal) . If your POS terminal does not have a customer-facing display , please contact our support team to have your automatic surcharges enabled. In this case, your staff will still be prompted to choose between credit or debit during the check out flow. Surcharges do not currently apply to: Split transactions Orders placed at kiosks

articles.body: Overview This feature enables you to split a customer's order payment between multiple credit/debit cards, or between card and cash. How It Works When checking out a customer, you can choose to split the payment between two or more cards, or between card(s) and cash. Here’s how: 1. Select “Split Payment” At the payment method selection screen, tap Split payment . 2. Choose How to Split You’ll be prompted to either: Enter a specific dollar amount for the first payment, or Split the total evenly between a number of customers or payment methods. You can split an order total into a maximum of five separate transactions. 3. Collect the First Payment After entering the amount or selecting how to split, the POS will prompt you to collect the first payment. If tipping is enabled, each partial payment will also prompt the customer to leave a tip. Tip suggestions will be based on the partial amount. 4. Continue with Remaining Payments After collecting the first payment, the system will prompt you to collect the next. If splitting between cash and card, use the left-hand menu to toggle between payment methods. 5. Complete the Transaction Once the total amount has been paid, the screen will show $0.00 remaining . Receipts & Cancellations A separate receipt is printed for each partial payment. Each receipt will indicate it was a partial payment . If you cancel during the payment process, all pending transactions will be voided , and a cancellation receipt will print. Viewing Split Payments In POS Order History Split payments will show up as multiple linked transactions for a single order. ⚠️ If you process a refund for a split payment, all associated transactions will be refunded together . articles.body: When issuing a refund through the POS, it's important to note that tips are not automatically refunded . If a tip was added to the original order, you'll need to manually include the tip amount in the refund process. 🧾 Example Scenario Let’s say a customer’s total order (including a tip) was $100 , and you processed a refund for only $80 . If the customer later reports that they didn’t receive the full refund, it may be because the tip amount (e.g., $20) was not included in the original refund. ✅ How to Refund a Tip on the POS Locate the order in the POS Order History . Select "Issue with order" Check the boxes next to the items you are refunding. Look for the “Staff Tip Refunded” field — this field is editable . Unlike other refund functionality, you will need to type the amount you are refunding in. It will not refund the tip automatically if you refund the order. If you intend to refund the tip, enter the tip amount in that field. Complete the refund. 💡 Tip: The “Staff Tip Refunded” field must be manually filled out. If this field is left blank, the customer will not receive a refund for the tip portion. 🔁 Can I Refund the Tip Later? Yes. The option to refund the tip remains available on the POS for up to 7 days after the original order . Even if the base order was already refunded, you can still return to the same order and issue a separate refund for the tip. 📌 Important Notes Always verify the refund total before confirming, especially when a tip was included in the original payment.

articles.body: What is Merchant Daily Payouts? Daily Payouts is a premium feature that allows you to opt-in to receive daily payouts (excluding weekends) for sales completed on the DoorDash platform 3 days in arrears. Currently, merchant payouts are issued weekly on Thursday for sales completed the previous Monday-Sunday. How can I opt-in and opt-out of Daily Payouts? You can opt-in to Daily Payouts via the merchant portal. 1. To opt-in, go to the Settings page in your Merchant Portal . 2. Within this window, you will see a button with the prompt Get Daily Payouts towards the bottom 3. If you wish to opt-out, you can do so on the settings page as well. You should see a button with the prompt to ‘Opt-out of Daily Payouts’ which can be used to return to a weekly schedule. What sort of notifications will I receive? When enrolled in Daily Payouts you will receive an email each day a payout is received confirming that funds have been transferred. These emails will include a breakdown showing which orders went into the payout, the total net payout you are receiving, and any adjustments that impact the total payout. By opting in to Daily Payouts, you will not receive a weekly report email. How will I be paid out when transitioning to Daily Payouts? When you first enroll in Daily Payouts, your first payment will include any accrued unpaid amounts up to three days prior to enrollment. How can I review my payout history? Payments are visible on the ‘Payments’ page in the merchant portal. This is also where you would review payments on a weekly pay schedule. Will I be charged for this feature? DoorDash does not charge for Daily Payouts. If this becomes a paid program in the future, we'll provide sufficient advanced notice and opt-out ability. articles.snippet: With Time Tracking, you can track employee hours, breaks, tips, and wages in one place, giving you the data you need for accurate payroll and compliance. articles.body: With Time Tracking, you can track employee hours, breaks, tips, and wages in one place, giving you the data you need for accurate payroll and compliance. These tools give you clear visibility into shifts and simplify payroll, whether you process it manually or work with a bookkeeper. Opening Time Tracking: Go to Point of Sale > Time Tracking in your Merchant Portal. View Shifts: In the Shifts table , you’ll see: Live and ongoing shifts of clocked in employees Paid and unpaid breaks Credit card tips collected by employee Total paid hours Use filters to focus on specific employees or date ranges. Edit Shifts: If you need to edit or add an employee shift, you can do it here. Simply click the shift in question to make updates. Then, you can: Add or change a break type (paid or unpaid) Adjust clock in and out time Adjust paid vs. unpaid time Note: If an employee forgets to clock out, they will be automatically clocked out after 24 hours. If this happens, you will need to follow the above steps in order to correct their hours. Configure Break Types In Settings , you can set up to three break types. Click the pencil on the righthand side of one of the breaks to make edits. There are several configurable settings within each break, including: Break name Fixed time vs. Indefinite Paid vs. unpaid Enabled and disable break Once enabled, the breaks will be available for your employees on your POS. Lastly, across all breaks, there is a toggle to convert excess time from a paid break to an unpaid break. For example, if this is toggled on: Lunch break duration : 30 minutes Clock out: 12:00 PM Clock in: 12:36 PM (36 minutes) The excess 6 minutes will automatically be converted to unpaid time when the employee clocks back in at 12:36 PM. Export Data Use the Export option to download detailed shift summaries, including hours, breaks, and payment details. Using Time Tracking on the POS Clock In and Out From the employee passcode screen on the POS (and before they enter their passcode), the employee will press Clock In/Out. They will then be prompted to enter their employee passcode. Once they enter their passcode, they are automatically clocked in. Take Breaks When an employee wants to start a break a break, they select a break type . Breaks are logged as either paid or unpaid, based on your settings. When they return from their break, they simply navigate back to the employee passcode screen, press Clock In/Out and select End Break. Review Shift Summaries From the Reports tab, click Employee Sales Report where you can review, by date and time, employee shift lengths, sales, and credit card tips. Anyone with access to this report can also Clock Out themselves or other employees directly from this page. Press Print (in the upper right-hand corner for a printout of these reports on your POS printer. Frequently Asked Questions How do I set or edit break types? Go to Settings in your Merchant Portal to configure up to three break types. Where do I find tips or paid hours? Check the Shifts table in your Time Tracking tab. Why does the POS ask employees to select a break type? This ensures that break time is tracked accurately for payroll and compliance. How do I export a shift summary? Select the Export option in either your Merchant Portal or print it from the POS.
