articles.title: Item-Level (Product Mix) Reporting
articles.snippet: You can view detailed, item-level reporting in both your Merchant Portal and the Business Manager app (BMA) . These updates are designed to give you deeper insight into how individual menu items are performing — helping you make smarter decisions about inventory, pricing, and menu changes. 📊 Overvie
articles.body: You can view detailed, item-level reporting in both your Merchant Portal and the Business Manager app (BMA) . These updates are designed to give you deeper insight into how individual menu items are performing — helping you make smarter decisions about inventory, pricing, and menu changes. 📊 Overview The Product Mix report shows performance data for every menu item you sell. You can use it to understand which items drive your sales, identify trends over time, and compare performance across stores or channels. You’ll find key metrics such as: Total Sold – the total quantity of each item sold Gross Sales – total sales value before discounts Item Errors – the number of orders with issues related to that item Discounts – total discounts applied to that item You can access this data at either the store level or the business level, depending on how your account is set up. 💻 Using the Product Mix Report in Merchant Portal Go to the Insights tab → Select Product Mix . At the top of the page, use the date range selector to choose the time period you want to review. (Optional) Select a comparison range to see how item sales have changed over time — the report will automatically show the percent change in item count and gross sales between the two periods. Use the filters to narrow results by: Channel (e.g., POS, Delivery, Pickup) Store (if viewing at the business level) Sort any column by clicking its header — for example, you can sort by gross sales or total sold to see your best-performing items. Search for specific items using the search bar at the top of the report to quickly find what you need. These tools let you customize the view to focus on exactly the insights that matter most to your business. 💡 About the “Popular” Tag You may notice a “Popular” designation next to certain items in your Product Mix report. This label reflects item popularity based on sales activity in the Merchant Portal over the past 30 days — not just in-store performance. Because it takes into account Merchant Portal ordering trends, your top 10 “Popular” items may not always match your top 10 best-selling in-store items. This broader view helps you understand what customers are most frequently purchasing across all channels. 📱 Viewing Item-Level Data in the Business Manager App You can also access your Product Mix report directly from your phone: Open the Business Manager app . Tap the More tab at the bottom of the screen. Select Product Mix . From here, you can apply similar date and channel filters as in the Merchant Portal. You can also tap on any individual item to see detailed performance metrics for that specific product — all from your mobile device. 📥 Downloading Your Product Mix Report You can now download a CSV file of your item-level (Product Mix) data directly from the Merchant Portal. This makes it easier to review your data offline or share it with your accounting or inventory teams. To download your report: Go to the Insights tab → select Product Mix . In the upper right corner, click Download CSV . The file will download automatically and include all item-level data from the Product Mix view you have open. The download will reflect any filters or date ranges you’ve applied in the Merchant Portal. For example, if you select a custom date range or filter by channel, your CSV will include only that filtered data. ⚠️ Download Limitations CSV downloads are only available through the Merchant Portal. You won’t see a download option in the Business Manager app. This new Download CSV button replaces the older Product Mix report available in the Operations Report Builder , which relied on outdated item-level data. For the most accurate and up-to-date item-level insights, use the new Product Mix Download CSV option in the Merchant Portal. 🧠 Why Use This Report While item-level data may have been available in older dashboards or custom reports, the new Product Mix report is the most accurate and up-to-date source for product-level insights on DoorDash. 🛠 No Setup Required There’s nothing you need to do to enable these updates. The new Product Mix report is already available in your Merchant Portal and Business Manager app . If you have questions or feedback about your reports, please contact pos-support@doordash.com or reach out through your standard support channel.

articles.body: Self ordering kiosks are designed to make in-store operations faster and more efficient while also improving the guest experience. By allowing customers to place their own orders, kiosks reduce wait times, increase accuracy, and free up staff to focus on other tasks. Restaurants may also see higher check sizes thanks to built-in upsell prompts. Hardware Setup Each kiosk includes: Floor-standing kiosk mount with a 22-inch touchscreen tablet, or Countertop kiosk mount with a 15-inch touchscreen tablet Connected Stripe payment terminal for secure, card-based transactions Connected guest receipt printer for instant order confirmation Customer Ordering Journey 1. Kiosk Home Page Guests are greeted with a customized restaurant home page . Supported dining options (e.g., Dine In or Take Out ) are displayed clearly. 2. Building the Cart Guests browse the menu, select items, and personalize orders using the touchscreen. A timeout feature resets the screen back to the home page if inactive, keeping the kiosk available for the next customer. 3. Checkout & Upsells Before paying, guests see recommended add-on items ("Complement your cart") , which can be added to the cart without navigating back to the menu. This step may help increase average order value while keeping the flow seamless 4. Payment Guests follow on-screen prompts to complete payment at the connected Stripe terminal. Upon successful payment, the kiosk displays a confirmation message and prints a receipt for the customer. Order Fulfillment As soon as an order is placed, kitchen tickets are automatically printed at the appropriate prep stations. Tickets include all item details and any special instructions entered by the guest. Why It Matters Self ordering kiosks benefit both restaurants and customers: For restaurants: reduced labor costs, faster throughput, more accurate orders, and higher check sizes. For guests: shorter waits, full menu visibility, easy customization, and smoother checkout. Interested in adding a kiosk setup to your restaurant? Contact your Account Manager for more info and pricing.

articles.body: ⚙️ Auto Degraded Mode Degraded Mode allows your POS to continue operating when you lose internet connectivity. With the new Auto Degraded Mode feature, your POS can now automatically detect an internet disconnect and switch into offline functionality — helping you stay up and running with minimal disruption. 💡 General Functionality What is Degraded Mode? Degraded Mode is your POS’s offline mode. It allows your staff to continue taking orders even when your POS is offline or if DoorDash is experiencing an outage. What is Auto Degraded Mode? Auto Degraded Mode automatically turns on your POS’s offline functionality when it detects that your device has lost internet connectivity. How do I know if Degraded Mode is on? You’ll see “Degraded mode enabled” in your POS status bar. In low or no-internet scenarios, this will usually appear alongside a strikethrough Wi-Fi symbol and a red status bar . How will I know when I’ve exited Degraded Mode? Once your POS reconnects to the internet, the “Degraded mode enabled” message will disappear and your status bar will return to its normal color (black). You will also see a WiFi symbol without a strikethrough. Does this change how DoorDash manually pushes me into Degraded Mode? No — DoorDash may still push your POS into Degraded Mode during a system-wide issue. When this happens, your POS will display “Degraded mode enabled” , but you may not see the Wi-Fi strikethrough icon since your local connection could still be active. ⏱️ Timing Limitations I lost internet, but Auto Degraded Mode didn’t trigger — how can I enter it? You can still turn on Degraded Mode manually by going to Settings → Degraded Mode → Toggle On: If you do this manually, a 15-minute time limit applies. Once your POS recognizes that you’re offline, that time limit no longer applies. If you enter degraded mode automatically, the 15-minute time limit does not apply Why is there a delay before Auto Degraded Mode turns on? Your POS checks for internet connectivity at regular intervals. While this usually happens every few seconds, it can occasionally take up to 3 minutes to detect a full disconnect. That delay is expected and outside of DoorDash’s control. Offline Order History When your POS is offline and enters degraded mode, the Order History tab behaves differently than it does when you’re online. Offline Order History lets your team keep working without staring at a blank screen—but it has clear limitations you should be aware of. What you will see while offline You’ll see orders placed on that specific POS during the offline period . These orders will populate immediately on the Order History tab and remain visible until the device reconnects. What you won’t see while offline Offline Order History does not sync across devices while you’re offline. This includes: Orders placed on another POS at your location Orders placed on a kiosk Orders coming from online ordering channels (DoorDash Marketplace, Storefront, OLO, etc.) Uber Eats orders (for merchants using UE scraping) During an outage, each device is effectively operating on its own island. Only once every device is back online will orders sync and appear across devices. This usually happens within a few minutes of full reconnection. Common scenarios and what they mean “I’m offline and can’t see orders placed on another POS.” This is expected. While offline, Order History only shows local (same-device) orders. Once all devices reconnect, the orders placed elsewhere will appear automatically. “I’m offline and don’t see kiosk orders.” Kiosk orders won’t show until your POS is back online and the system can sync them. “I’m offline and don’t see DoorDash online orders.” Online orders cannot sync to your device during an outage. Expect them to load once your devices reconnect. “I’m offline and don’t see Uber Eats orders.” UE-scraped orders only sync when your devices are online. They’ll appear shortly after full reconnection. If only one device is offline If one POS shows degraded mode while others look normal, that POS alone is having connectivity issues. This is common and can be caused by: Cabling differences Local hardware issues Localized Wi-Fi drops or interference Orders placed on the offline POS will not appear on your online POS devices until it reconnects. What Offline Order History does not solve This feature does not change the existing limitations of degraded mode: Card readers may not work offline Printers may fail to print offline Gift cards, split pay, and scheduled orders are still unsupported while offline If these functions stop working, it’s due to the broader constraints of degraded mode—not Offline Order History. Reconciliation Once Back Online When your devices regain internet connectivity, the POS automatically reconciles any orders that were created or received while a device was offline. This process is entirely system-driven — no manual action is needed — but it’s important to understand what will happen and when. How reconciliation works Local offline orders (orders placed on the same POS): These remain visible the entire time and simply sync their final status (e.g., payment, fulfillment) to the cloud once you're back online. Orders placed elsewhere that did not appear offline: Once all devices are online, the POS fetches any missing orders and updates the Order History list. This includes: Orders from your other POS devices Orders from kiosks Marketplace / Storefront / third-party online orders Uber Eats scraped orders Typical timing: Reconciliation usually completes within a few minutes of full connectivity being restored across all devices. What you should expect after reconnection Order History will populate with all missing orders: Anything that was invisible offline will appear automatically once the device syncs. Order timestamps will reflect the original time of creation , not the time your POS came back online. Fulfillment and payment details will normalize once synced with the cloud (e.g., credit card status, item-level details). When reconciliation may appear “slow” Reconciliation is delayed if: One or more devices at the location are still offline A POS reconnects but has unstable connectivity (frequent drops) A kiosk is online but the POS is not (or vice versa) The system waits for all devices to be online long enough to sync cleanly. In practice, this usually resolves within a few minutes of stable internet returning. 🚫 Limitations My card reader stopped working in Degraded Mode — what’s happening? Auto Degraded Mode does not enable offline card processing. If your internet is down, your card reader will not function. For now, you can process payments manually (e.g., Manual Card Entry ) Note: Offline card reader support is planned for a future update. My printers stopped working in Degraded Mode — what’s happening? Degraded Mode does not include offline printer support. If your printers rely on Wi-Fi, they may stop working during an outage. For now, please write tickets manually . Offline printer support is planned for a future release. Gift cards, split pay, or scheduled orders aren’t working — is that expected? Yes. These features are not supported in Degraded Mode. Our team plans to expand offline feature support over time. My internet is weak, but Degraded Mode didn’t activate automatically — why? Auto Degraded Mode only triggers when your POS detects a full disconnect . If your internet is unstable or weak but not fully disconnected, you can manually enable Degraded Mode from Settings . 🖥️ Kiosk Behavior Does Auto Degraded Mode work on kiosks? Not yet. Kiosk Degraded Mode functions differently since kiosks cannot accept manual card payments. When a kiosk goes offline, it automatically displays a “Please order at the counter” message once a customer interacts with the screen. Can I still manually display the “Please order at the counter” message? Yes. Go to Kiosk Settings → Degraded Mode → Toggle On. The manual toggle is time-limited to 15 minutes. My POS is in Degraded Mode, but my kiosk is still processing orders — why? Your kiosk is likely still connected to the internet. This can happen if your kiosk and POS use different cabling or network paths. It’s not an error and does not indicate a broader issue. 🔧 Setup and Configuration Do I need to enable Auto Degraded Mode? No action is needed — this feature is already turned on for all POS devices. Can I disable Auto Degraded Mode? No, this feature cannot be disabled. If you’d like to share feedback about why you want it disabled, please contact Support — we’ll pass it along to our product team. What happens if I try to turn off Degraded Mode while offline? Your POS will automatically re-enter Degraded Mode within a few seconds once it detects that you’re still disconnected.

articles.snippet: We're always here to help, but here are some helpful tips you can try when issues come up with the POS or other devices. 1. Check Physical Connections Cables : Inspect all cables for damage and ensure they are securely connected. Look for frayed wires or loose connections. Power : Confirm that all n
articles.body: We're always here to help, but here are some helpful tips you can try when issues come up with the POS or other devices. 1. Check Physical Connections Cables : Inspect all cables for damage and ensure they are securely connected. Look for frayed wires or loose connections. Power : Confirm that all networking devices (routers, switches, modems) are powered on and have appropriate indicator lights. Network Interface : Check the network interface (Ethernet port or Wi-Fi adapter) is functioning properly on the affected device. For the POS this can be found on the base of the stand behind the front plate. For the Kiosk this can be found by opening the door and attached to the back of the tablet. 2. Restart Devices Restarting devices can resolve many connectivity issues by refreshing the network configuration. Router/Modem: Unplug the power, wait 30 seconds and plug it back in. This action can clear errors and re-establish connections. DoorDash Devices: Restart the affected device to refresh its network settings. 3. Check Network Configuration For Cabled Connections: Ensure the device is able to obtain an IP address automatically (DHCP) This can be found in Android Settings through the control panel. To access the Control Panel: Press the two buttons on the back of the tablet. (Note: this will tell you if you are Online, Offline, or Online (Not Provisioned) Swipe up Enter password tq68vk Press the hamburger menu in the top right corner Press Settings Enter password 1DoorDash Press Android Settings Select Networks & Connections Verify that the correct network is enabled. For Wireless Connections: Confirm that the Wi-Fi is enabled on the device and that the correct network (SSID) is selected. Check the Wi-Fi password for accuracy. 4. Firewall and Security Settings Firewalls or security software can block network access. This is usually the culprit if we are receiving the Online (Not Provisioned) error in the Control Panel. Temporarily Disable: As a diagnostic step, temporarily disable the firewall to see if it resolves the issue. Check Settings: Ensure that the firewall is configured to allow necessary applications and services. 5.. Seek External Help If you have exhausted all troubleshooting steps and the issue persists: Reach out to DoorDash In-store Support through our text line or email . Contact ISP: Reach out to your Internet Service Provider (ISP) for assistance. They can check for outages or network-specific issues. When reaching out to our team, videos showing a suspected bug are extremely helpful in our investigation. We'll likely go over the above troubleshooting steps, and ask some clarifying questions: What is the specific issue (i.e., system lag, no connection)? When did the problem start? Are multiple devices affected or just one device? Have any recent changes been made?

articles.body: The Network Debugger is a tool to view the traffic going over the network, and thus independently check the validity of that traffic. It can be used to view the status of your internet connection and test your download speed. 1. Go to “ Settings ” in your tablet and select “ Network Debugger. ” 2. Select “Start” Connection Type: Ethernet/WiFi Download Speed: The rate that digital data is transferred from the Internet to your computer. Latency: is the amount of time it takes for a data packet to go from one place to another. Packet Loss: occurs when one or more transmitted data packets fail to arrive at their destination. _________________________________________ How to Use This Information to Troubleshoot Issues Understanding the information shown in the Network Debugger can help you diagnose common network-related problems that might be affecting your POS system or other connected services. Slow or Unreliable POS Performance: If you're noticing delays when taking orders or processing payments, check the Download Speed . A slow speed could indicate that your internet connection is struggling to keep up with real-time demands. In this case, try restarting your router and the switch. If the problem persists, you may need to contact your internet provider. Frequent Disconnects or Timeouts: High Latency can cause your device to lag or time out. If you see latency numbers well above 100ms, this could explain why certain apps or functions aren't working smoothly. Try relocating your router closer to the tablet or reducing the number of devices connected to the network. Missing or Incomplete Data (e.g., orders not going through): If you notice Packet Loss , it means some of your network data isn’t making it to its destination. This can result in missing or corrupted order data. Packet loss often points to a poor or unstable connection—consider having your ISP investigate further. By checking these values in the Network Debugger, you can rule out or confirm whether your network is contributing to performance issues. If everything looks normal and you're still experiencing problems, share a screenshot of the Network Debugger results with Support—this will help us troubleshoot more effectively.

articles.title: Understanding the New Status Bar on DoorDash POS
articles.snippet: What is the new status bar? The new status bar appears at the top of your DoorDash POS screen and gives you real-time visibility into: Your card reader connection status Your offline payment availability and remaining limit Other device connectivity (printers, internet, customer display) The status
articles.body: What is the new status bar? The new status bar appears at the top of your DoorDash POS screen and gives you real-time visibility into: Your card reader connection status Your offline payment availability and remaining limit Other device connectivity (printers, internet, customer display) The status bar is now interactive, so you can click the status bar to get a full view of your device health status. It’s designed to help you quickly understand your system’s health—especially during connectivity issues. What information does the status bar show? Depending on your setup and current conditions, the status bar may display: A connected or disconnected card reader indicator A notice when your system enters degraded (offline) mode Your remaining offline payment limit (when applicable) Alerts if key devices (printers, customer display) disconnect You can tap the status bar at any time to see more detailed information. Offline payment limit visibility When your POS is offline and accepting offline payments: You have a $7,000 limit per offline session The limit resets once your system comes back online The remaining balance only appears in the bar when it drops below $1,400 , to reduce distraction during normal operation If the limit is reached, card payments will be temporarily blocked until your system reconnects. Card reader status indicators No message shown: Your reader is connected and working normally Disconnected: The reader may be powered off, on a different network, or physically disconnected Updating: Your reader is installing a routine software update (this usually takes a few minutes) During updates, you may need to use manual card entry temporarily. Can I turn the status bar off? No. The status bar is a core system feature and cannot be disabled. What information isn't shown in the status bar show? The status bar currently does not provide explicit troubleshooting steps you can take to reconnect devices experiencing intermittent connectivity issues. In most cases, device connectivity can be restored by simply turning the device off, waiting a few seconds, and turning it back on. If issues persist, you are always encouraged to reach out to our team. If something looks wrong If you don’t see the status bar or tapping it doesn’t open details: Pin out of the POS Pin back in If issues persist, contact DoorDash POS Support.

articles.body: No Power Use this guide when your Elo device does not respond when turning on the system. Check that the power cable is properly connected to the wall and your POS device. Verifying the physical connection will require removing the faceplate beneath the POS. If there is a screw holding this piece in place, you will need a screwdriver to remove it. If you have a z30 model, usually indicated by an integrated customer-facing display (your customer screen is part of the POS base), you will be looking for the circular port at the top of the base, beneath the faceplate. If you have z20 model, usually indicated by an attached or detached (separate) customer-facing display (your customer screen is part of the POS base), you will be looking for the circular port at the top of the base, beneath the faceplate. Next, check the power LED status on the underside of the POS. If the power LED is solid white, then the system is ON. If the power LED is red/amber , then the system is OFF. If the system has no light, it may not be receiving power. To attempt troubleshooting, unplug the power cable and then plug back in after five seconds. Blank Screen If the power button LED is blinking, the system may be in SLEEP mode. Press the power button to bring the unit out of SLEEP mode.

To troubleshoot the WisePOS E if it's not connecting to your POS terminal, first ensure it's connected to the internet. The upper right hand corner of the device should sh
articles.body: Connectivity issues between device and the POS We use Stripe WisePOS E credit card terminals with a USB-C powered charging dock. To troubleshoot the WisePOS E if it's not connecting to your POS terminal, first ensure it's connected to the internet. The upper right hand corner of the device should show one of two symbols if it's connected: A WiFi symbol, which indicates an active WiFi connection An ethernet symbol <->, which indicates an active Ethernet connection. For the POS to connect to the reader, both devices must be on the same network, so you will need to ensure your devices are on the same network NOTE: It is OK if the POS is on ethernet and the reader is on WiFi, but they must still be on the same network. For example, if Router A has the WiFi Network "My Restaurant WiFi" and and your reader is connected to "My Restaurant WiFi," your POS will still connect to the reader if your POS is hardwired (via ethernet) to Router A. The same device is providing an internet connection to both devices. To check connectivity , go to settings (swipe right, enter the Admin PIN: 07139), and then select Wi-Fi settings. This displays all available Wi-Fi networks. To see more details about the connection, tap on the connected network name. If they are not on the same network, you will need to set the devices to be on the same network. If your reader is on the same network as the POS, the next thing to try is a simple restart: Hold down the power button on the right side of the device. A pop up should appear that asks if you want to restart the device or shut down. Press restart and the device will restart Upon relaunching, any software updates will be installed. Do not press any buttons while this is happening. The reader will launch back to your standard screen once the restart is complete. Test the connection by attempting to check out a credit card transaction. Issues with inserting a card Check to see that the WisePOS E has power Make sure nothing is blocking the card slot Make sure the card's chip is facing the right direction when inserting the card Issues with tapping a card Check to ensure that the credit card supports NFC (near field communication) payments Cards capable of NFC will have this symbol on them: Make sure the credit card is placed within a 4-centimeter range on top of the NFC symbol on the reader's display Make sure the customer takes the NFC payment card out of a wallet or purse when a payment is made to avoid any interference

articles.body: Overview We use Star Micronics ethernet based printers. Our printers are diagnosed through the Power and Error lights which are called Error Indicators. The error and the power lights will blink at different intervals which will mean a different type of error. In order to troubleshoot the printer you need to identify the error If you are still experiencing issues with your printer after troubleshooting or the error has been determined “Non-Recoverable,” please contact DoorDash support Using WiFi Printing If you are one of our WiFi printing merchants and are having any issue, please navigate to the StarQuickUtilitySetup app from the AppStore and following the triaging steps within their app Identifying printer issues using lights You can troubleshoot many common issues using the lights on the front of the printer. Below are errors that can be resolved with the recommended fix or general troubleshooting you can find below: _________________________________________________________________________________ Power is Off Power off status. Turn On/Off Power Power is On and Ready Power is on and the ready status is enabled. WiFi Setup is Running WPS is running. Connect Tablet/PC WiFi Setup Connection Failure WPS connection failed after 120 seconds. Check that the router or access point to connect to is in WiFi Protected Standby status and try the WPS connection again. Connect Tablet/PC Link Down/Disconnected Connection with destination router or access point was disconnected. Check the network status. Connect Tablet/PC Link Down/Cannot find IP The IP address cannot be obtained. If a DHCP server is used, check operations of the DHCP server. If a DHCP server is not used, reach out to support in order to set a proper IP address. Connect Tablet/PC Stops printing due to detected high temperature for the head Since the printer head temperature is high, printing has stopped. When the printer head temperature returns to a normal range, printing will resume automatically. Cover open error The printer cover is open. Set the paper, close the printer cover, and it will move to the ready status. The Ready LED will display according to the network link display. (The figure indicates the ready status) Paper Setup Out of paper error The printer is out of paper. Set the paper, close the printer cover, and it will move to the ready status. Be sure to remove the plastic core from the previous roll before installing the new roll. The Ready LED will display according to the network link display. (The figure indicates the ready status) Paper Setup Cutter Error The cutter did not operate properly. If a paper jam is happening, remove the paper that is causing the jam after turning off the power, and move the movable part to the home position by referring to Cutter Lock . If the same error is displayed even after the movable part is moved, contact support.

articles.body: General networking overview Consistent cable management is important for your POS system’s performance. articles.title: Loyalty Program Overview and FAQs
articles.snippet: Loyalty Program Overview What is it: Your new loyalty program lets customers earn and redeem points whether they're ordering in-store, on your website, or through DoorDash—and they don’t need to use DoorDash to participate. It’s designed to keep your customers coming back by rewarding them every tim
articles.body: Loyalty Program Overview What is it: Your new loyalty program lets customers earn and redeem points whether they're ordering in-store, on your website, or through DoorDash—and they don’t need to use DoorDash to participate. It’s designed to keep your customers coming back by rewarding them every time they order. How does it work: Customers can sign up for loyalty via online ordering, DoorDash app, or directly at the POS by entering their phone number. This program is spend based, so after they spend $X, they’ll earn $Y in rewards. Customers can easily accrue and redeem rewards in-store, and the more they spend, the more they earn! Signup for Rewards Step Instructions Image 1 The customer will see their total on the customer facing POS screen and complete their payment, including the tip. After that, the customer-facing screen will prompt them to sign up for loyalty by entering their phone number 2 The customer will receive an SMS with a link to create their loyalty profile If the customer has a DoorDash account : Click the “Link with DoorDash” button This will create a loyalty profile linked to their DoorDash account Customers can view their reward progress and redeem rewards directly in the DoorDash app If the customer doesn’t have a DoorDash account : Select “Complete Profile.” Enter the required information (email and name) to create a loyalty account Note: this link will not show real time rewards status, see below how to check rewards Accrue Rewards Step Instructions Image 1 On their next in-store order, before they have earned a reward, the customer-facing POS screen will display the total. The customer will pay using a credit card, which the POS will recognize to automatically track their spending towards rewards progress. They will also receive a text confirming that their purchase contributed to their rewards Redeem Rewards Step Instructions Image 1 On their next in-store order, once they have earned a reward, the customer-facing POS screen will display the total. The customer will pay using a credit card, which the POS will recognize and allow the customer to use the reward on that purchase or save it for later. 2 If the customer has completed their rewards account: the customer-facing POS screen will allow the customer to proceed to add a tip, and the payment will be complete with the reward amount deducted 3 If the customer has not completed their rewards account: the customer-facing POS screen will display the terms and conditions for review. The customer can close this prompt, proceed to add a tip, and the payment will be complete with the reward amount deducted Frequently Asked Questions Can customers accrue and redeem points online? Yes, they can accrue and redeem on the DoorDash app, your restaurant’s online ordering or in store. Can Customer Accrue and redeem points on a Kiosk No, the ability to accrue and redeem points and awards is not currently available for in-store Kiosks. In-store redeeming and accrual must be done at the POS at this time and cannot be with cash. My customer is unable to redeem a reward online (DoorDash app or Online Ordering) Ensure the customer is logged in on DoorDash or Storefront and does not have any other promotions applied Ensure the customer has created a rewards profile, they can do this by logging into online ordering or DoorDash Ensure the Cx is not purchasing alcohol If this does not work, contact DoorDash using the contact info below What happens if my customer gets a new phone number? The customer will need to create a new account. Contact DoorDash using the contact info below to have points transferred from one phone number to the other. Why do customers need to create a profile? Creating a profile allows customers to view their reward progress and redeem rewards across all channels: DoorDash, Online Ordering, and in-store. Customers who have not created a profile can still earn rewards but will not be able to redeem them until their profile is completed. What if the customer doesn’t create a profile right away? The POS will show that they have earned a reward and allow them to opt in on the customer facing screen Can customers use these points at other restaurants on DoorDash? No, points accrued through this loyalty program can only be used at your restaurant(s) on loyalty What happens when a customer orders and then cancels their order? The spend amount will be automatically deducted from their rewards progress If my customer uses cash to pay, will it count towards their loyalty progress? At this time, cash cannot be used towards rewards progress If a customer saves their rewards, can they combine them on a future purchase? No, the customer cannot stack rewards, they will need to use their rewards on separate future purchases Is spend contributed towards rewards calculated before or after tax and tip? Spend contributed towards rewards progress is calculated before tip is added Can multiple cards be linked to a loyalty account? Customers can link multiple cards to a single loyalty profile. The key identifier is the phone number or DoorDash account , not the card itself. If a customer uses a new card without linking it via the phone number, it will create a separate rewards track . Once they enter the same phone number , the new card gets linked and all rewards merge under one profile .
